s: Which of the following groupings has a Senior Cyber Group for cybersecurity partnership with India?

s: What score did India get in the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024?

s: The Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy 2017, implemented by APTS, has how many verticals?

s: Into which of the following does the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 group countries?

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Barriers which are directly connected with the sender and receiver is said to be:
Right to Privacy is contained in:
x: Article-21 The Right to Privacy has been held to be a part of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21. This was affirmed by the Supreme Court in the landmark K.S. Puttaswamy judgment (2017). The ruling recognised privacy as a fundamental right implicit within the broader guarantee of Article 21.

s: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement? Indian Polity: Constitutional Framework PMF IAS IP – 14
o: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and freedom guaranteed in Part III
x: TH Amendment to the Constitution The Right to Privacy was recognised as a fundamental right by the 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017). The Court held that the right to privacy is intrinsic to the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, which is part of Part III of the Constitution of India, dealing with Fundamental Rights.

s: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India?
x: The Right to Privacy is protected under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty. This was affirmed by the Supreme Court in the landmark Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India judgment (2017), where a nine-judge bench unanimously held that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 and is also connected with the freedoms guaranteed under other fundamental rights.

s: Article 21 of Indian Constitution secures
o: Right to life, personal liberty and right to privacy
x: Article 21 secures the right to life and personal liberty, and in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) the Supreme Court held privacy to be intrinsic to them. So option 4 is correct, while options 1-3 each leave something out.

s: How many judges unanimously decided K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, which recognised privacy as intrinsic to life and liberty?
x: A unanimous nine-judge bench held privacy protected under Article 21 and Part III.

s: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh to the extent that those decisions had done which of the following?
o: Recognised proportionality as the sole test for all restrictions
Denied the existence of privacy as a protected constitutional interest
Declared education to be a Directive Principle
x: Puttaswamy overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy as a constitutional protection.

s: A government measure restricts personal data without any supporting law, although it claims to pursue a public objective. Which requirement of the privacy test is most clearly absent?
x: The legality requirement demands that an intrusion into privacy be supported by a law. A claimed public objective cannot substitute for the existence of legal authority.

s: Which of the following case–proposition pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kharak Singh v State of UP – Privacy recognised as a Fundamental Right
Gobind v State of MP – Privacy recognised as part of personal liberty
Puttaswamy v Union of India – Early recognition of privacy concerns under Article 21
Kharak Singh v State of UP – Informational privacy affirmed
x: Gobind v State of MP (1975) treated privacy as part of personal liberty. Kharak Singh (1962) was overruled by Puttaswamy insofar as it denied privacy, so it did not recognise privacy as a Fundamental Right. Puttaswamy (2017) was not an early case: its nine judges unanimously held privacy a Fundamental Right under Article 21.

s: In which case were safeguards on interception of communications in India laid down?
o: Kharak Singh v State of UP (1962)
K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017)
Shreya Singhal v Union of India (2015)
x: Interception safeguards come from PUCL v Union of India (1997), not Kharak Singh.

s: On which date was K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India decided?
x: The nine-judge Puttaswamy judgment came on 24 August 2017; 26 September 2018 is the Aadhaar judgment.

s: Which 1975 case held privacy to be part of personal liberty?
x: Gobind v State of MP (1975) treated privacy as part of personal liberty.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution did the Supreme Court in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) place the right to privacy?
x: Puttaswamy held privacy to be intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and Part III.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: What is the position of Andhra Pradesh amongst all the States in terms of percentage of SHGs with credit linking to Bank out of total SHGs?

Justice K. Venkataswami resigned from the post of the head of the Commission of Enquiry of Tehelka.com regarding corruption in defence purchases. Who was appointed in his place as the head of the Commission?
Who dissented in the 4:1 Aadhaar judgment of 26 September 2018?
x: The five-judge Bench decided 4:1, with Justice D.Y. Chandrachud dissenting.

s: Which Aadhaar linking was upheld in the Aadhaar judgment (2018)?
o: Mandatory linking with both bank accounts and SIMs
x: PAN/ITR linking under Section 139AA was upheld; mandatory linking with bank accounts and mobile SIMs was struck down.

s: Which of the following was NOT upheld in the Aadhaar judgment (2018)?
x: Section 57 private-entity use was struck down; the Act, welfare use and PAN/ITR linking were upheld.

s: How many judges delivered the Aadhaar judgment of 26 September 2018?
x: The Aadhaar bench had 5 judges (4:1), unlike the 9-judge Puttaswamy bench.

s: Which body prepared the 2018 draft personal data protection Bill?
x: The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee drafted the 2018 Bill (2017-18), before the 2019 PDP Bill, its 2022 withdrawal and the 2023 DPDP Act.

s: The 2021 Joint Parliamentary Committee report on the Personal Data Protection Bill proposed how many amendments?
x: The 2021 JPC report proposed 93 amendments and covered both personal and non-personal data; the Bill was withdrawn in 2022.

s: With which of the following is the Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee associated?
x: The Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee dealt with non-personal data; A.P. Shah with privacy, Srikrishna with the PDP Bill and A.K. Bhargava with net neutrality.

s: In which year was the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019 withdrawn?
x: The 2019 Bill was withdrawn in 2022, before the DPDP Act of 2023.

s: Who headed the 2012 Group of Experts on Privacy?
x: Justice A.P. Shah headed the 2012 Group of Experts on Privacy.

s: Who headed the 2015 DoT committee on net neutrality?
x: A.K. Bhargava headed the net neutrality committee; A.P. Shah headed the privacy experts group.

s: In which year did the Digital Personal Data Protection Act receive Presidential assent?
x: The DPDP Act received assent on 11 August 2023, after the 2019 Bill was withdrawn in 2022.

s: In which year was the Personal Data Protection Bill referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
x: The PDP Bill, 2019 was sent to a JPC in 2019; the JPC reported in 2021 with 93 amendments.

s: Which kind of data is excluded from the DPDP Act, 2023?
o: Data of foreign entities offering goods in India
x: The DPDP Act excludes non-personal data, though it covers entities outside India offering goods or services in India.

s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, who is the Data Principal for a child under 18?
x: For a child under 18, the parent or guardian is treated as the Data Principal, not the Data Fiduciary.

s: Which of the following is NOT an additional obligation of a Significant Data Fiduciary?
o: Appointment of a Data Protection Officer in India
Automatic exemption from all consent requirements
x: A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a Data Protection Officer in India, appoint an independent auditor and undertake impact assessment. It does not receive an automatic exemption from consent requirements.

s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, what is a Consent Manager?
o: A government officer who investigates cybercrime
A registered entity through which a Data Principal gives, manages and withdraws consent
An auditor appointed only by a Significant Data Fiduciary
A tribunal hearing appeals from the Board
x: A Consent Manager is a registered entity enabling a Data Principal to give, manage and withdraw consent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the DPDP Act, 2023 and the GDPR?
o: The DPDP Act covers only digital personal data, whereas the GDPR covers all personal data.
Both frameworks use the term 'Data Fiduciary' for the entity deciding the purposes of processing.
The DPDP Act provides for financial penalties only.
Data portability is an explicit GDPR right but not a statutory right under the DPDP Act.
x: The GDPR uses 'Data Controller'; 'Data Fiduciary' is DPDP Act terminology.

s: What is the GDPR term for the DPDP Act's 'Data Fiduciary'?
x: A Data Fiduciary decides purpose and means of processing, like the GDPR's Data Controller.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. It covers only digital personal data.
2. It also applies to foreign entities offering goods or services in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The DPDP Act covers only digital personal data and also reaches foreign entities offering goods or services in India.

s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised right of a Data Principal under the DPDP framework?
o: Right to impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary
x: The listed rights include information and access, correction, erasure, grievance redress, withdrawal of consent and nomination. A Data Principal does not impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary.

s: The right to erasure of a Data Principal is in which section of the DPDP Act?
x: Erasure is in Section 12 of the DPDP Act; under the GDPR it is Article 17.

s: Which of the following is a duty of a Data Principal under the DPDP Act?
x: Data Principals must not give false information, impersonate or file frivolous complaints.

s:
Consider the following statements about children's data under the DPDP Act, 2023:
1. Verifiable parental consent is needed for persons below 18.
2. Targeted advertising at children is barred.
3. Behavioural monitoring of children is permitted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Parental consent is needed below 18 and tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads are barred, so statement 3 is false.

s: Under the DPDP framework, below what age is verifiable parental consent required?
x: Verifiable parental consent is needed below 18 years; tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads aimed at children are banned.

s: Which of the following receives no exemption under the DPDP Act, 2023?
x: Journalism gets no exemption; notified State agencies, research, archiving and statistics can be exempted.

s: Which section of the DPDP Act, 2023 contains the 'legitimate uses' that allow the State to process personal data without consent?
x: Section 7 covers legitimate uses; Section 17 lets the Centre exempt notified State agencies on grounds of sovereignty, security and public order.

s: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act was amended by which provision of the DPDP Act, 2023?
x: Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act amended Section 8(1)(j), letting authorities refuse all personal information and removing the public-interest override.

s: What did the DPDP Act's amendment of RTI Section 8(1)(j) remove?
x: Section 44(3) lets all personal information be refused and removes the public-interest override.

s: Which section of the DPDP Act provides for exemption of notified State agencies?
x: Section 17 lets the Centre exempt notified State agencies; Section 7 covers legitimate uses.

s: In August 2026, to which bench was the challenge to the DPDP Act's amendment of RTI Section 8(1)(j) referred?
o: A Full Bench of the Delhi High Court
x: The challenge to Sec. 44(3) amending RTI Sec. 8(1)(j) was referred to a Constitution Bench in August 2026.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Out of the following, currency note of which new denomination is recently released by RBI?
Under the DPDP framework, what is the maximum penalty for breach of obligations regarding children's data?
x: Children's data obligations carry up to ₹200 crore; additional SDF duties ₹150 crore and residual breaches ₹50 crore.

s: What is the maximum penalty for failure to take reasonable security safeguards under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act?
x: Failure of reasonable security safeguards may attract a maximum penalty of ₹250 crore.

s: Where do appeals against decisions of the Data Protection Board of India lie?
x: Appeals lie to TDSAT; the Board is headquartered in New Delhi and its members are appointed by the Central Government.

s: Who appoints the members of the Data Protection Board of India?
x: The Centre appoints Board members; appeals lie to TDSAT.

s: What is the maximum penalty for breach of Significant Data Fiduciary duties under the DPDP Act?
x: SDF breaches carry up to Rs 150 crore in the 250-200-150-50 crore ladder.

s: What is the maximum penalty for a Data Principal breaching her duties under the DPDP Act?
x: Breach of Data Principal duties attracts up to Rs 10,000.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Data Protection Board of India?
x: The Data Protection Board, an adjudicatory body under the DPDP Act, has its headquarters in New Delhi.

s: What is the maximum penalty for a residual breach of the DPDP Act, 2023, not covered by a specific head?
x: The penalty ladder is 250-200-150-50 crore; residual breaches carry up to Rs 50 crore.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: "Pegasus Allegations" Committee, constituted by the Supreme Court, is headed by...
When were the final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules notified?
x: The final DPDP Rules were notified on 14 November 2025; 3 January 2025 was the date of release of the draft Rules.

s: Which of the following sets of practices is in line with the DPDP Rules?
o: Clear and specific consent, plain-language notices and purpose limitation
Consent without information, unrestricted collection and unlimited reuse
Implied consent, technical notices and indefinite retention
Anonymous consent, no retention controls and compulsory foreign storage
x: The Rules require clear, specific and informed consent, plain-language notices, purpose limitation, data minimisation and retention controls.

s: Who supervised the Supreme Court-appointed technical committee in the Pegasus matter?
x: Justice R.V. Raveendran supervised the committee, which found malware on 5 of 29 phones but could not conclusively link it to Pegasus.

s: Under the DPDP Rules notified on 14 November 2025, by when is full operational compliance due?
x: Full compliance is due 18 months after notification, in May 2027; Consent Manager provisions come in November 2026.

s: What do India's first national standards for cloud, data centres and ethical AI focus on?
x: The standards focus on bias, data sovereignty and privacy and are linked to the DPDP Act; spectrum auction pricing is not among them.

s: When did RBI issue the mandate requiring all payment-system data to be stored only in India?
x: The RBI's April 2018 mandate required all payment-system data to be stored only in India.

s: How does the DPDP Act treat transfer of personal data outside India?
o: Permitted only to countries approved by the RBI
Permitted except to countries restricted by the Central Government
x: The DPDP Act follows a blacklist (negative-list) approach: transfers are allowed unless the Central Government restricts particular countries.

s: Under the DPDP Rules 2025, from when do the Consent Manager provisions apply?
x: Consent Manager provisions apply from November 2026; full compliance is due by May 2027.

s: When were the draft DPDP Rules released?
x: The draft came on 3 January 2025 and the final Rules on 14 November 2025.

s: The Supreme Court's Pegasus committee found malware on how many of the 29 phones examined?
x: Malware was found on 5 of 29 phones, though not clearly Pegasus.

s: How does the GDPR regulate cross-border data transfer?
x: GDPR uses a whitelist/adequacy model; the DPDP Act uses a blacklist.

s: AP Police's AI4AP pilot, which raises DPDP issues, covers which districts?
x: The AI4AP pilot covers Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya.

s: Which of the adopted following a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
x: The GDPR is a legal framework that establishes rules for the collection and processing of personal data of individuals within the European Union (EU). The regulation was put into effect on May 25, 2018. It requires individuals to give explicit consent before their data can be processed.

s: Which of the following adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
x: In April 2016, the European Union (EU) adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' (GDPR) and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018. It replaces the EU Data Protection Directive of 1995. GDPR standardizes data protection law across all EU member countries and imposes strict new rules on controlling and processing personally identifiable informations (PIIs). This regulation also extends the protection of personal data and data protection rights by giving control back to EU residents.

s: Which of the following is true of the Right to Be Forgotten as understood in India?
o: Applies only to biometric data collected by UIDAI
Limits name-based searches without necessarily erasing judicial records
Automatically cancels the judgment of a court
Prohibits every search involving the person's name
x: The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.

s: Under which Article of the GDPR is the Right to be Forgotten formalised as the 'Right to Erasure'?
x: The GDPR's Right to Erasure is Article 17; RTBF originated in Google Spain v. AEPD (2014), and the DPDP Act gives a Right to Erasure under Section 12.

s: The Right to Be Forgotten began with which case?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017)
x: The Right to Be Forgotten began in Google Spain v AEPD (2014).

s: The GDPR replaced the EU Data Protection Directive of which year?
x: The GDPR replaced the 1995 Directive.

s: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) of the European Union was implemented from which date?
x: The EU GDPR, adopted in April 2016, was implemented from 25 May 2018.

s: Which of the following correctly contrasts penalties under the EU GDPR and India's DPDP Act, 2023?
o: GDPR provides administrative fines and lets member states add criminal penalties; the DPDP Act provides financial penalties only
GDPR provides criminal penalties only; the DPDP Act provides imprisonment
GDPR has no fines; the DPDP Act provides both fines and imprisonment
x: The GDPR itself prescribes administrative fines (up to EUR 20 million or 4% of global turnover) and lets member states lay down other, including criminal, penalties; the DPDP Act, 2023 provides financial penalties only.
